The player must first locate an acacia door (marking the entrance to a small farmhouse/cottage), then find a potted red tulip inside or near the structure (requiring them to enter through the door), and finally mine carrots from a garden plot accessible only after navigating past the tulip area. This creates a natural spatial dependency: navigate to structure → explore interior → harvest crops. All tasks are observable, verifiable, and require no deep Minecraft domain knowledge — just exploration and basic interaction.

Max distance of 5 blocks ensures the player must be inside or at the back of the house to satisfy this — they cannot see it from outside the front door (the tulip is ~5 blocks from the door at the back-left corner). Facing tolerance of 60 degrees confirms they are looking at the tulip.

Uses inventory_has because mining mature carrot crops (age=7) drops carrot items directly into the player's inventory. The item type is 'carrot' (singular, no minecraft: prefix). Requiring min_count of 1 means the player has successfully broken at least one mature carrot crop and collected the drop. No tools are needed — carrots can be broken by hand in survival mode. The player starts with an empty inventory so any carrot in inventory confirms mining.

The player spawns south of the house on a grass field with a cobblestone path leading to the front door. The farmhouse has glass pane windows, a crafting table, and a chest inside. The carrot garden has 15 fully mature carrot crops on hydrated farmland with a water source.
task_text: Find the farmhouse with the acacia door. Go inside and locate the potted red tulip. Then find the carrot garden next to the house and harvest some carrots.
